subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Living Root Bridges: Nature as Engineer
description: A fast breakdown of Living Root Bridges: Nature as Engineer for builders.

hook.text: In Meghalaya, India, bridges grow. They're made of living tree roots trained across rivers over decades.

buildup.text: The Khasi people guide Ficus elastica roots through hollow betel nut trunks toward the opposite bank.

discovery.text: After 15 to 30 years, roots interlock and thicken. The bridge strengthens with age — the opposite of steel.

twist.text: Some living root bridges are 500 years old and can support 50 people at once. They outlast any steel bridge.

climax.text: Researchers are studying bio-engineering to grow structures. Nature solved problems we're still working on.

punchline.text: The best bridge doesn't decay. It grows.

quiz.question: How do living root bridges differ from conventional bridges over time?
options: They slowly dissolve and must be regrown every decade
They get stronger with age instead of weakening like steel
They only work in tropical climates near the equator
